seo.title: Keep Singing for Palestine — Sept 19 Street Rally | Gangjeong Peace and Music Camp
seo.description: Saturday 19 September 2026, 17:30, Gwanghwamun Square area. Gangjeong Peace and Music Camp joins a street rally singing against the deployment of South Korean troops and for the liberation of Palestine. Previous bookings are closed and will be refunded in full.

intro.heading: We keep singing
intro.para_1: Rooted in the peace movement of Gangjeong Village on Jeju Island, now in its 19th year, Gangjeong Peace and Music Camp has gathered the will to oppose war and to resist through the language of music.
intro.para_2: This time we bring the songs of peace that rang out in Gangjeong Village to Seoul, to share them together.
intro.para_3: To stand with Korean civil society fighting against Israel's 78-year illegal occupation of Palestine and its genocide, we keep singing without pause!

rally.heading: From the rally to the concert
rally.body: At 14:00 we join the Emergency Action of Korean Civil Society in Solidarity with Palestine with a solidarity performance by Namsu, a versatile solo artist. Join us from the rally all the way to the concert!

lineup.heading: The people who sing
lineup.subheading: Four acts singing in the streets for the liberation of Palestine

ihyeongju.name: Lee Hyeong-ju
ihyeongju.description: A singer-songwriter rooted in fingerstyle blues, weaving folk and jazz into his music. Since 2017 he has taken part in the New Minjung Music Compilation vols. 1–3 and sung at sites of social violence. Debut EP Atopy (2019), full-length album We Wanted to Keep Each Other (2023).

notice.heading: Gangjeong Peace and Music Camp is taking to the streets and the squares
notice.subheading: Against the US–Israeli war of aggression on Iran and the deployment of South Korean troops — on the change of plan for the Keep Singing for Palestine concert
notice.refund_body: Now that the 19 September concert at Banjul has become participation in a street rally, ticket bookings are closed. The organising committee will contact everyone who booked, one by one, and refund the full ticket price. There is no need to apply — please wait for us to reach you.
notice.para_1: In March this year, the United States and Israel invaded Iran. From the earliest days of the war, Trump demanded that South Korea send troops. The government, which at first said it was not considering a deployment, has recently shifted to saying it is "reviewing various options with the national interest as the top priority."
notice.para_2: A rally against the deployment was accordingly held in Seoul on Saturday 12 September. Taking that as our starting point, we must now organise as many citizens as possible before Chuseok and show sustained momentum against the deployment. With the current government’s approval rating continuing to fall, the cry of the people gathered in the square is both an effective way to stop the deployment and the last line of defence against South Korea becoming a perpetrator in the war of aggression on Iran.
notice.para_3: The organising committee of the Gangjeong Peace and Music Camp had planned to hold a peace concert in solidarity with the Palestinian liberation movement on Saturday 19 September at Banjul in Seoul. But the committee judged that this moment calls for more than solidarity through music — it calls for going out into the square and acting together with our fellow citizens. We are therefore changing the plan for the Keep Singing for Palestine concert.
notice.plan_1: On 19 September we will hold a rally in the streets of Seoul where music and speech together carry our opposition to the deployment and our hope for the liberation of Palestine.
notice.plan_2: We will take part in the rally against the deployment and, as soon as it ends, hold a guerrilla peace concert.
notice.plan_3: We will join the emergency action rally of Korean civil society in solidarity with Palestine with performances and speeches, and march in the Climate Justice March under our banner.
notice.plan_note: The confirmed time, place, and lineup are below.
notice.para_4: The colonial rule and genocide inflicted on the Palestinian people and the war of aggression against Iran launched by the United States and Israel are by no means separate matters. They are tragedies of the same order and a chain of acts of aggression, in which imperialist militarism tramples the lives and peace of people and justifies violence. To sing for peace in Palestine is to oppose the war of aggression against Iran, and it is firmly tied to stopping the deployment of South Korean troops.
notice.para_5: Now, when we fear the deployment motion will be tabled before Chuseok, only the voices of the people gathered in the square can stop this dangerous war of aggression from running out of control. The Gangjeong Peace and Music Camp takes up the power of solidarity that music carries and goes out to the streets and the squares. Join us, so that songs for the liberation of Palestine may ring out as one with the cry against the war on Iran and against sending South Korean troops.
